title: Introduce Prefill 'ghost' scenario simulator and quant profile exporter
author: Asha Verma
description:
Context and motivation: Customers and internal tenant simulations often need to understand how different prefill strategies, cache sizes and quantization tiers interact before rolling changes into Dedicated/Private clusters. Existing prefills were tested with simple traffic replays; we lack a compact, deterministic runner that can synthesize tenant-level cold/cold-to-warm transitions and export compatible quant profiles for downstream deployment. This PR adds a lightweight 'ghost' scenario simulator that (1) runs sampled prefill scenarios deterministically, (2) produces compact telemetry artifacts (batch shape histograms, cache hit traces, kv-cache footprints), and (3) emits an opinionated quant profile export that can be consumed by the optimizer pipeline.
Design summary: - New package pkg/prefill/ghost: deterministic runner with scenario definitions. Scenarios are small YAML files (samples included) that define tenant traffic mix, sequence length distributions, and warm/cold windows. - CLI integration via redwoodctl prefill run-ghost: lets operators run local quick simulations and output a tarball with telemetry.json and quant_profile.yaml. - Quant exporter in pkg/quant/exporter: takes steady-state token statistics from the simulator and produces an annotated quant_profile.yaml with recommended quant tiers and fallback thresholds for per-layer quantization. - Telemetry adapter: telemetry/metrics/prefill.go emits a compact telemetry envelope compatible with our ingestion pipeline (prefill.* metrics and prefillsim.batch_shapes histogram).
Files changed (high-level): - cmd/redwoodctl/prefill.go: add run-ghost command wiring and flags (-scenario, -seed, -output). - pkg/prefill/ghost/ghost_sim.go: core simulator, deterministic RNG, scenario interpreter, warmup/warmdown logic. - pkg/prefill/ghost/scenarios/sample_profiles.yaml: sample scenarios for quickstarts. - pkg/quant/exporter/export.go: quant profile generation and heuristics. - telemetry/metrics/prefill.go: metric export helpers and envelope serialization. - docs/prefill/ghost-runner.md: user-facing guide and examples. - test/e2e/prefill_ghost_test.go: e2e smoke tests and deterministic checks. - ci/pipelines/ghost-sim.yml: lightweight CI job for simulator lint/test. - internal/config/samples/prefill_profiles.yaml: seed scenario samples used by integration tests. - Makefile, go.mod updates for new packages.
Checklist: - [x] Simulator core implementation and deterministic tests - [x] CLI wiring and quickstart scenario - [x] Quant exporter and header annotations - [x] Telemetry envelope and ingestion smoke test - [x] Unit + e2e tests - [x] Documentation and quickstart examples
Backwards compatibility: The simulator and exporter are additive. Quant export format uses a new top-level key 'redwood_quant_profile_v1' to avoid confusion with older downstream parsers.
Migration notes: When using exported quant_profile.yaml in a live rollout, follow the normal canary flow (create a compact quant variant, run traffic shadow for 24h, then canary).
Implementation notes and tradeoffs: - The simulator intentionally does not attempt to emulate GPU kernel-level scheduling; it produces higher-level signals (batch sizes, cache hits, kv footprint) and a conservative quant suggestion. The goal is early-stage signal for tenant owners, not final production calibration. - Quant heuristics are conservative: prefer higher precision when observed per-layer token variance is high. - The CLI includes a --dry-run mode that prints top-5 quant suggestions without producing artifacts.
Security and privacy: Scenario YAMLs must not include PII; sample scenarios are synthetic. Telemetry envelope redacts any tenant identifiers by design and tags runs with a local-run marker.
CI and validation: The initial CI run failed due to a race in the deterministic RNG seeding; fixed by replacing global rand with a seeded xorshift64+ in ghost_sim.go. Final CI status: all unit tests and e2e smoke passed on linux/amd64.
Release notes: "Add a tool (redwoodctl prefill run-ghost) to simulate tenant prefill scenarios and export a conservative quant profile to aid rollout planning and cost optimization."
Related work: follow-ups include hooking this output into the autotune pipeline (ENG-7605) and adding a UI surface in the Console for one-click simulation (PM-412).

review_comments: Noah Patel: Nice approach. Two requests: (1) can we make the scenario schema stricter (explicit max/min fields for seq length)? (2) please add a short note in docs about how this differs from existing replay-based prefill.
Asha Verma: Responded - added stricter schema and validation in scenario_parser.go; doc updated with comparison section and example outputs.
Priya Singh: Found a potential N+1 when serializing envelope in telemetry; prefer streaming encoder. Also request small unit test to assert redaction of tenant IDs.
Asha Verma: Switched to json.Encoder streaming API and added test redaction_test.go. CI flake was due to RNG; replaced with xorshift64+.
Marco Rossi: Approving - flagged a follow-up for Console integration (PM-412) and a telemetry retention question; OK to merge after CI green.
GitHub Actions: CI run #42 - initial unit failing tests (race) -> fixed in commit 6; final run passed all checks.
release_notes: Added 'redwoodctl prefill run-ghost' simulator and quant exporter to help teams preview cost/quality tradeoffs before rollout. Produces a telemetry bundle and a conservative quant_profile.yaml for downstream autotune or manual canaries.
notes_for_oncall: This change is additive; the simulator writes only to the provided output path. If customers run the tool in dedicated/private clusters, ensure their telemetry ingestion policy allows prefill.* metrics. The exporter uses conservative defaults; any sudden production regressions should be investigated by disabling new quant tiers in rollout and reverting to pinned model variants.
smoke_test_result: e2e smoke: passed (deterministic scenario run produced identical batch-shape histogram across repeated runs with the same seed)
manual_steps_documented: docs/prefill/ghost-runner.md includes quickstart: run 'redwoodctl prefill run-ghost --scenario sample_profiles.yaml --output /tmp/ghost-output.tar.gz --seed 42' and then inspect quant_profile.yaml
